title: SDK compatibility notice & staged upgrade orchestration playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Create a customer-facing playbook and changelog guidance specifically focused on SDK breaking/behavioral changes across LTS and minor releases. This playbook complements existing migration templates by: listing affected SDK versions, providing precise code-level migration snippets, defining staged rollout gates, and offering targeted comms for developer platforms (NPM, PyPI, Maven) and enterprise customers. Deliverables: a set of channelized message templates (email, in-console banner, changelog entry, release notes), a compatibility matrix for SDK + runtime versions, a step-by-step migration checklist for customers, and a rollout timeline with rollback criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix published to docs.redwood.ai linking SDK semver ranges to runtime and model variants
Three channel templates (email, console banner, release notes) reviewed and approved by legal and support
Migration guide contains code diffs for JS/Python/Go SDKs and passes developer testing with sample apps
Rollout gates defined and automated signals configured in Console for 'canary-fail' and 'gradual-increase' policies
Stakeholders (support, SEs, developer advocacy) have run tabletop with the playbook and provided feedback
comms_templates: Email subject (general): Important: Redwood Inference SDK compatibility notice for console-2026.04

Email body (short): We will begin a staged rollout of console-2026.04 on 2026-04-15. This release includes SDK surface changes that may affect users on SDK versions older than 3.2. See the migration guide: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk-migration and the compatibility matrix: https://docs.redwood.ai/compat-matrix
In-console banner (urgent): 'Action required: Update Redwood SDK to >= 3.2 before 2026-05-01 to avoid deprecated authentication behavior. Learn more' -> links to migration steps

Release notes snippet: 'Behavioral change: the streaming API now returns chunked events for tool-calls. Impact: clients using custom stream parsers may need to handle new 'tool_event' frame. Example fix in JS SDK included.'
Enterprise escalation template: Outline of impact, suggested mitigations, rollback window, contact info, and SLA implications for Dedicated/Private customers
changelog_guidance: Format: Summary line (1 sentence), Impact (none/low/medium/high), Affected SDK versions, Migration quickfix, Link to full migration guide

Example entry: 'Streaming frame change (medium): JS SDK < 3.2 fails to decode new tool_event frames. Upgrade to 3.2+ or add stream parser fallback. Quickfix: replace 'parseStream(v)' with 'parseStream(v, {legacyMode: true})'. Full guide: /sdk-migration#streaming-frames'
We will annotate each changelog item with 'Customer impact' and recommended 'Immediate action' so Support can triage faster
Changelog distribution: central changelog (docs site) -> weekly release digest -> targeted emails for affected customers
migration_steps: Identify: Use Console usage filters to find customers using SDK < 3.2 or custom streaming parsers
Contact: Send targeted email + in-console banner to affected customers 30 days before enforced changes
Provide artifacts: create code diffs for JS/Python/Go showing minimal changes and a runnable sample app repository
Offer automation: ship a migration script for token/session rotation and a compatibility test suite customers can run
Staged rollout: enable change for 5% of traffic (canary) -> 25% -> 100% with automated health checks (error rate, latency, customer-reported issues)
Rollback criteria: if canary error-rate increases by > 2x baseline OR 3 enterprise customers report P1 regressions, pause rollout and revert behavior flag
Post-rollout: run a 14-day stabilization window and publish a 'post-upgrade impact report' summarizing incidents and mitigations
